text:
maria: starting a canary for peko-18b int4 today. goal: get perf baseline and check memory frag/coldstart behavior. hitting OOMs on coldstart about 10% of runs on canary hosts. logs in stackdump channel.
sam: can you paste the exact error? coldstart OOM or allocation failure during kv init?
maria: allocation failure when priming kv cache and allocating prefetched tensors. stack shows failure in allocator at 0x7f.., then GPU OOM on select contexts.
kai: any pattern on sequence length or max_new_tokens? sometimes defaults blow up with long prompts.
maria: most repros use user prompt ~1k tokens + max_new_tokens default 1024. we suspected the default.
leah: 1024 default seems high for 18B int4. we usually land at 256/512 for canary. 1024 with prefetch=on will try to reserve massive KV and warmup slots.
noah: can we confirm whether prefetch reserve is enabled? config on canary shows `prefetch.reserve_ratio: 0.25` and `prefetch.max_new: 1024`.
sam: reserve_ratio 0.25 * 1024 ~ 256 tokens worth of reservation per request — multiplied by batch concurrency it adds up.
maria: yes. also observed fragmentation after heavy canary runs — memory not reclaimed well between sessions.
kai: sounds like two things: (1) over-aggressive max_new default + prefetch defaults -> big allocations; (2) allocator fragmentation with int4 kernels. propose reducing defaults for peko-18b.
leah: propose action items: 1) lower `service.default_max_new_tokens` for peko-18b to 256 in canary. 2) set `prefetch.reserve_ratio` to 0.1 for canary. 3) enable soft-evict on idle KV after 200ms idle. 4) add a canary metric for fragment ratio and OOM count.
sam: +1. also add a temporary per-route override so customers can opt in to 1024 if they want.
maria: did a quick bench: with defaults (1024, reserve 0.25) p50=120ms p95=650ms token/sec=180. after lowering to 256 & reserve 0.1 p50=95ms p95=380ms token/sec=210 and no OOMs in 200 test runs.
noah: quality check? any generation regression from reducing max_new_tokens default? that only impacts allowed max generation length, not model quality for short responses.
leah: risk is callers who rely on long generations by default. but we can preserve behavior via explicit route config. default should be safe.
kai: another mitigation: change prefetch strategy from eager to windowed (only prefetch N tokens ahead based on upstream latency profile). less reservation, similar latency.
maria: true. I'd like to roll default change first (256 + reserve 0.1) and monitor for errors and customer impact.
infra-bot: deploy job queued: canary-config-update/prefetch-tweak (job id cj-5860). will report back on completion.
sam: also add a small allocation defrag: call `cudaDeviceSynchronize(); malloc_trim()` style or run a light defrag between heavy sessions. We have a kernel to trigger compaction.
oah: on the model side, ask quant team if int4 kernel has high slab fragmentation; maybe use slab allocator with larger block sizes for peko.
leah: opened GH issue: rw-infer/alloc#432 "peko-18b int4 fragmentation and prefetch reservation". linked the bench results and logs.
maria: next steps: - roll canary config change (maria) - perf monitor dashboard (sam) - quant team q/a on block sizes (kai) - add per-route override doc (leah). aim to finish in next 48h.
sam: I will add a temporary SLO: block peko routes with >2 OOM/hour from canary.
kai: for reproduction, here's a minimal repro snippet we used:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "peko-18b-int4",
  "prompt": "<~1000 token prompt>",
  "max_new_tokens": 1024,
  "prefetch": true
}
```
use loadtool with concurrency 3 to repro quickly.
maria: FYI: quality regression question popped up in evals: some longer-context QA threads had truncated answers when we forced 256 default. we'll publish guidance to increase max_new per-route for those workloads.
oah: also recommend an autoswitch: if request.prompt_length + requested_max_new > 1500, fall back to windowed prefetch or ask the runtime to require explicit override.
leah: good idea. we'll consider gating large requests to dedicated nodes only.
maria: will update thread when canary deploy finishes. thanks all :pray:
